chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadeed from Jamil ibn Darradj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who buys food, then sells it before he takes possession of it, he said: 'There is no objection.' And if a man authorizes the buyer from him to measure it and take possession of it, he said: 'There is no objection.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell food before taking possession of it in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of selling food before physical possession (qabd), a key issue in the jurisprudence of bay' al-ma'dum (sale of non-existent goods). It further validates the mechanism of delegation (wakalah), allowing the buyer to measure and take possession on the seller's behalf, thereby resolving practical ambiguities in commercial transactions. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia fiqh in facilitating trade while maintaining contractual integrity.
